issues.issue: Rights are said to be 'forfeitable in the event of certain circumstances or occurrences as herein set forth' without identifying which circumstances, leaving the forfeiture trigger to be assembled from elsewhere. The phrase 'certain circumstances or occurrences' has no ascertainable content on its face.

On assignment the clause says 'this Licensor shall then have no responsibility or liability... whatsoever to Licensee,' a garbled sentence ('this Licensor') whose subject and effect are unclear. Whether the assignor or the assignee is released turns on that slip.

The support promised — 'Monthly seminars in Minneapolis, Minnesota, Telephone Consultation and Email Support' — is stated without any measure of frequency, scope or responsiveness for the consultation and email limbs. What performance discharges the obligation is not fixed.

The requirement of 'trained medical personnel on site daily in the form of either a DC, DO, MD, PT' is a closed list whose exclusion of other credentialed staff is uncertain, and the exclusivity ban on 'any other type of physical therapy, training or rehabilitative service' is drafted without limit. Whether a clinic's ordinary practice breaches it is contestable.

'Perform in a professional manner,' 'any reasonable guidelines issued by ARP Wave' and conduct that 'reflects favorably' are standards with no benchmark stated in the Agreement. Whether conduct breaches them cannot be resolved from the words.

The restraint is bounded by 'the Territory defined in the Exclusive Licensee Agreement executed by the parties,' but no Exclusive Licensee Agreement forms part of this instrument and no Territory is defined anywhere in it. The geographic scope of the covenant therefore cannot be determined from the contract as a whole.

The prohibited activity — representing 'any similar or competitive system or Licensee' — is both garbled ('or Licensee') and unbounded ('similar'), so the conduct restrained is not identifiable. A two-year post-termination restraint of that width invites construction against the drafter.

The $1,400 monthly license fee duplicates the 'ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS' charge on the cover page and the 'PROTOCOLS $16,800.00' line in the lease Rent clause, and its duration depends on the blank term in Section 6.1. Whether one obligation or several were created is not clear from the instrument.

Both the effective date and the expiry date are left blank, and the sentence reads 'shall be continue in full force and effect until unless otherwise terminated,' which is ungrammatical and leaves no ascertainable term. The duration of the license cannot be read off the clause.

Only Licensor is given a right to terminate here, which cannot be squared with Section 6.3's automatic termination events or with the one-year term stated in Paragraph 1 of the Equipment Lease. How long the license runs depends on which of these controls.

Providing that all 'covenants and provisions herein set forth shall survive such termination, except those covenants as pertaining to future payments' makes the whole agreement perpetual in substance, and the exception's boundary ('future payments') is undefined. Which obligations genuinely survive is open.

Blanket survival is hard to reconcile with Section 2.2, under which the right to operate lasts only 'during the term,' and with Section 11.2, which requires immediate return of all Systems on termination. Read literally, terminated obligations both end and continue.

'Or other adverse creditor action' is a catch-all appended to the enumerated judgment, levy, lien, attachment and foreclosure notice, and its reach beyond those specifics is uncertain. Automatic forfeiture turns on where that general phrase stops.

Default may be declared 'if Licensor deems itself insecure,' a wholly subjective trigger with no reasonableness standard, and default under 'any other agreement entered into between Licensor and Licensee' is unbounded. Whether a purported default is valid is left to be construed.

Venue is confined to 'the Hennepin County, Minnesota, Federal or State District Court,' but no federal district court sits for Hennepin County, so whether the District of Minnesota is a permitted forum is genuinely arguable. The scope phrase 'enforcement of this Agreement' also leaves tort and related claims uncertain.

The clause duplicates Section 21 of the Equipment Lease in slightly different words, so a single dispute arising under both halves of the instrument is governed by two overlapping venue provisions. The duplication is awkward rather than contradictory.

The License Agreement declares itself the entire agreement 'regarding the subject matter hereof,' while Paragraph 18 of the Equipment Lease says the Lease is the entire agreement between the same parties, and both are executed as one document. Which integration clause bounds the bargain is unresolved.

Requiring notices by facsimile or overnight courier conflicts with Paragraph 22 of the Equipment Lease, which allows personal delivery, telegram or first class mail. A notice of default touching both agreements could satisfy one clause and fail the other.

The carve-out for 'THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES, IF ANY, MADE IN THE ARP WAVE LEASE AND LICENSE AGREEMENT' must be read against the Lease's Warranty paragraph promising free repair of defects. Whether that repair promise survives this disclaimer is arguable.

The first sentence preserves claims for 'breach or breaches of Licensor's contractual obligations,' while the second waives all rights to claim 'fraud, inaccuracy, imperfection of the System(s)' — an exception and a waiver that overlap. How far the preserved contract claim survives the fraud waiver is unclear.

The disclaimer of any representation as to 'effectiveness... or usefulness of the System(s)' pulls against the recital that Licensor owns and licenses proprietary rehabilitative protocols and against Section 3's promised support. The tension is real but not plainly irreconcilable.

'Any rights herein set forth shall be deemed to be automatically revoked and automatically reassigned to Licensor' does not distinguish Licensee's rights from Licensor's, and rights never assigned to Licensee cannot be 'reassigned.' The class of rights reverting is not identified.

Automatic revocation of 'any rights herein set forth' on termination is hard to square with Section 6.2, under which all covenants and provisions survive termination. One clause extinguishes what the other preserves.

The Agreement contains no clause headed confidentiality or non-disclosure beyond the proprietary-rights language of Section 4.5, so which provisions this survival clause preserves is uncertain. The clause points at a category the instrument never labels.

Disclaiming any 'franchise' relationship sits uneasily with the operative scheme of trade-name use, mandated training, exclusivity and monthly fees created by Sections 2.2, 4.1 and 5. Whether the disclaimer controls the substance is a question a court could be asked.

The Guaranty covers 'all indebtedness and liability which Lessee/Licensee may have to Lessor/Licensor under this Lease Agreement,' though the instrument comprises both a Lease and a separate License Agreement with its own $1,400 monthly fees. Whether the license obligations are guaranteed turns on that single reference.
The guarantor is identified only as 'the undersigned' with the Guarantor signature line blank, so who is personally bound is not stated. That identity gap is the sort of thing litigated directly.
